name: NVIDIA Auto Ontology
what: Framework for semantic catalogs and ontology-backed natural-language queries over structured enterprise data.
edge: Shared metadata, definitions and provenance can ground agent analytics across connected data sources; product capability, not an independently measured accuracy advantage.
best_for: Evaluating governed, natural-language analytics over relational business data with cross-system definitions and lineage.
watch_out: Check generated SQL and database permissions. FastAPI trusts an identity header from an authenticated Next.js gateway and must remain an internal service. Without Vault, UI-added database credentials can be stored unencrypted in Postgres.
access: NVIDIA-authored code is Apache-2.0; separate third-party notices and model, source-database and hosted inference licensing or fees apply.
runtime: Docker Compose v2 or Kubernetes, Next.js, FastAPI Python 3.12+, PostgreSQL/pgvector, configured NVIDIA NIM endpoints and database credentials.
evidence_status: First-party code, README and licensing reviewed 2026-11-03; operation and model-quality claims not independently reproduced
notes: New to Atlas on November 3, not a November 3 product launch. Initial public release date unverified. Backend identity-header trust and plaintext credential fallback require special deployment care.
lifecycle: Source repository publicly documented; initial public release date unverified
comparison_basis: First-party documentation review, not head-to-head comparison or validated SQL correctness.
test_before_choice: Connect an isolated read-only test database; test query correctness against held-out known answers, RBAC, prompt injection controls, gateway isolation, credential storage and NIM usage cost.

name: Windmill
what: Code-first platform for scripts, scheduled jobs, APIs, workflows and internal apps, with optional agent and MCP integrations.
edge: Turns maintained scripts into workflows and human-facing apps with Git-based review and worker isolation; an available design capability, not an independently measured speed or security advantage.
best_for: Teams combining Python, TypeScript and SQL automations with internal forms, approval processes, integrations and auditable deployment review.
watch_out: A documented external-OIDC-token feature is not a security certification. Check issuer, token audience, role/workspace mapping, least privilege, secret access and worker isolation; review AI-generated code before deployment.
alternatives: Temporal for durable execution and stateful workflows
Apache Airflow for scheduled data pipelines
access: At v1.856.0, backend/frontend source is principally AGPLv3 with documented exceptions; clients and OpenAPI specs are Apache-2.0. Distributed Community Edition binaries include proprietary features and use/distribution limits; enterprise and commercial embedding/managed-service rights differ. Check the exact LICENSE before redistribution.
runtime: Self-hosting documented with Docker Compose or Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, server and separate workers; resource needs depend on job language, concurrency and workloads. Managed hosting, auth providers and optional secret backends have separate setup and costs.
evidence_status: First-party v1.856.0 release notes, tagged README and LICENSE reviewed 2026-11-03; feature operation, authentication security and performance not independently reproduced
notes: New to Atlas on November 3, not a new product launch. The November 2 v1.856.0 notes report external OIDC issuer access tokens for MCP, not universal support across all configurations; later versions may exist.
lifecycle: Existing software, source-reviewed at tagged v1.856.0; initial public release date not independently established
comparison_basis: Conceptual first-party feature comparison; no measured throughput, reliability or authorization-security benchmarks reproduced by Atlas.
test_before_choice: Deploy isolated test workers and a read-only demo integration. Check Git review gates, scoped OIDC access to MCP tools, user/workspace RBAC, secret handling, failure retries and job isolation; measure real workload latency and operational cost.
